 Michelle Dee withdraws from MGI All Stars; father says no crown is worth her health
 Marilag Odtohan ,
 ABS-CBN News
 Published November 19, 2026 11:19 PM PHT 
 Former Miss Universe Philippines Michelle Dee has withdrawn from the second edition of MGI All Stars following an emergency appendectomy, as she prioritizes her recovery.
 In a social media announcement, MGI All Stars confirmed Dee's withdrawal but said her place in the ongoing voting activity would remain, allowing fans to "continue showing their support and sending her encouragement throughout the campaign."
 The beauty queen previously shared an update on her recovery after being rushed to the hospital on November 9 due to a sharp, stabbing pain in the lower right side of her abdomen.
 Dee underwent an emergency appendectomy, which left three incisions in her abdomen. While the procedure was successful, she said her medical team advised her to strictly follow her recovery timeline and avoid prolonged strenuous abdominal activities and heavy exertion to prevent potential long-term complications.
 ADVERTISEMENT
 "Kilala niyo naman ako. Dapat buo, hindi kalahati ang mga laban sa buhay," she said, acknowledging that she would have to take things slower as she recuperates from a major surgery she "definitely wasn't expecting."
 The beauty queen also emphasized that she could not afford to rush her recovery or push her body beyond what it could safely handle.
 Following her update, several beauty queens sent messages of encouragement to Dee.
 Miss Universe 2023 Sheynnis Palacios left a message for the Filipina beauty queen, saying, "My Michelle! I hope you are well, take care of yourself."
 Meanwhile, reigning MGI All Stars queen Vanessa Pulgarin also expressed her well wishes, writing, "I hope you're well."
 ADVERTISEMENT
 In a separate post, Dee's father, actor Derek Dee, expressed pride in his daughter's pageant career, while reminding her that she had nothing left to prove.
 "With [MGI] All Stars just weeks away, my only wish is for you to take the time to heal and recover. The stage will always be there, but your health comes first," Derek said. 
 He emphasized that no crown was worth more than her health, underscoring the importance of allowing his daughter to recover rather than putting additional pressure on herself to compete.
 "Remember, your greatest victory is not a crown, but the beautiful person you are and the lives you continue to inspire," her dad wrote.
 Dee has established herself as one of the Philippines' notable pageant representatives, having competed in some of the world's biggest beauty competitions.
 ADVERTISEMENT
 She first won the Miss World Philippines crown in 2019 before representing the country at Miss World 2019 in London, where she finished in the Top 12.
 She returned to the national pageant scene in 2022 and was crowned Miss Universe Philippines Tourism. A year later, she earned the country's Miss Universe Philippines title, collecting several sponsor and special awards throughout the competition.
 At Miss Universe 2023 in El Salvador, Dee ended her journey with a Top 10 finish and brought home multiple special awards, including the Spirit of Carnival Award, Best in National Costume, Fan Vote Winner, and Voice for Change Gold Winner.
 Her return to the international pageant scene through MGI All Stars was seen as another opportunity to represent the Philippines, this time alongside fellow Reina Filipinas queens Alexie Brooks and Anne Patricia Lorenzo Diaz.
 The trio had been expected to challenge Pulgarin for the MGI All Stars crown at the December 12 competition.
 ADVERTISEMENT
 With Dee's withdrawal, Brooks and Diaz will now carry the Philippines' bid to dethrone the reigning Colombian queen.
 While Dee's absence changes the country's lineup, her recovery remains the priority as she takes time away from the competition to heal.
